note: The audit words a provider meets, each with one plain meaning and, where it helps, one or two more sentences shown only in the 'What these words mean' disclosure (REQ-025 FR-13; REQ-027 D-2709, D-2713). The one source: audit-kinds.json, the checklist's audit items, the home example and the result page read their meanings from here, so the site never carries two texts for one term. Written by the product owner on 15 October 2026 (REQ-025, with the review's decisions 16 and 17); NOT NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission text. Meanings read against the NDIS Act 2013, the Practice Standards Rules and the Worker Screening Rules on 16 Oct 2026 (product/qa/req-reviews/2026-10-16-glossary-read.md); every entry status reviewed.
author: readyline

items.meaning: an approved auditor checks your documents without coming to see you
items.more: The Rules call it a desk audit. The Commission calls these lower-risk supports.

items.meaning: an approved auditor reads your documents, visits where you work and talks to people
items.more: That includes you, your workers and the people you support. The Commission calls these higher-risk supports.

items.meaning: the quality rules in the law for registered providers
items.more: Which rules apply to you depends on the supports you provide or apply for. Your audit checks those.

items.meaning: a group of the Practice Standards rules on one topic
items.more: Which modules apply to you depends on the supports you deliver or apply for.

items.meaning: one thing an auditor looks for under a rule
a type of support you are registered, or apply, to provide
items.more: The law says 'class of supports'. The Commission's lists say 'registration group', with a four-digit code.

items.meaning: a second audit that most certification providers must have
items.more: The Rules say it must begin within 18 months of your registration starting, or later if the Commissioner allows. It covers your governance and management rules, anything under a corrective action plan, and anything the Commissioner names.

items.meaning: anything done that restricts the rights or freedom of movement of a person with disability
items.more: The law limits when and how it may be used.

items.meaning: the people who run the business or have a real say in how it is run, such as directors
items.more: Partners and board members count too (NDIS Act s 11A).

items.meaning: the part of the Commission's application where you show, with evidence, how you meet each rule
items.more: It is part of the online application and covers each rule that applies to you. Renewals have one too.

items.meaning: a check by your state or territory of whether a person is a risk to people with disability
items.more: Workers in risk-assessed roles need the clearance it gives, and so do key personnel and sole-trader providers, with few exceptions. Clearances last up to five years.

items.meaning: an incident the law and the Rules list, which a registered provider must report to the Commission
items.more: The list covers death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful contact or assault, sexual misconduct, and a restrictive practice used without authorisation or outside a behaviour support plan.

items.meaning: take a document as your own and date it
items.more: An auditor also looks for proof you follow it.
